[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: an 'interface' is a screen you click on, and documentation shows the code you type. SW rule: an API is a table of library methods, each line giving the method's signature (return type, name, argument types) and what it computes; the signature is not the code you type to call it.

[0] names_the_element (N): An API (application programming interface) is a table of library methods giving, for each, its signature and a short description of what it computes.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Each API line specifies the return type, the method name and the types of its arguments (the signature), plus a description; it provides the information needed to write a program that uses the method.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): To use an entry: find the method, read its signature left to right (return type, name, parameter types in order), write a call with the name and argument expressions of those types in that order, and use the returned value according to the return type (none for void).
[1] output_prediction (OP): From the API alone one predicts the type of a call's value: Math.sqrt returns a double, Math.round a long, Integer.parseInt an int, println nothing (void).
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Reading the API changes nothing in the program; it states what each call returns, and (for void methods such as println) what effect the call has instead of a value.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Each call must match one API signature: same name, arguments of the listed types in the listed order, and use of the value consistent with the return type.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): An API is a contract that separates the client, who needs only the signatures and descriptions, from the implementation; it lets programmers use large libraries without reading their code, and later to design their own libraries.

[0] predict_a_change (C): Client code keeps working when a method's implementation changes but its signature and behaviour stay the same; changing a signature (name, parameter types, return type) breaks every call that relies on it. Choosing which methods an API includes is a trade-off between convenience and size.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Consult the API whenever you use a library method (to get name, argument order and return type right); if no listed method fits, combine listed ones (e.g. secant from Math.cos) or write your own.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A call must match the API signature (argument types/number/order and return type). Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: Wrong argument types or count (Math.sqrt("2")), or a return value stored in an incompatible variable (int n = Math.round(x)).
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The API describes what the method returns; a value-returning call does not change its arguments. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Using a non-void method as a statement and expecting its argument to change (Math.round(x);).
StdAudio is a library used through its API of static methods.
StdDraw is a library used through its API of static methods.
An API lists, for each library method, the signature you need in order to call it: name, argument types and return type.
